admission.justification: Direct staging with after-the-fact restore and unvalidated commit were both built, measured and rejected on public state evidence across successive verification rounds; the choice binds every future converted adoption and its staging helpers.

alternatives.option: Prepare, stage and validate against a private copy of the worktree index; write the real index only after validation passes, and publish exactly the validated tree.
alternatives.reason: Dry runs, refusals and exceptions in the owned preparation/staging/validation interval leave the real index, concurrent staged edits and unowned files untouched by construction, while each error keeps its name. After validation passes, adoption publishes exactly the validated tree; a failure in that sanctioned publication retains its named error within the real-index state already preserved at validation, and the published bytes cannot drift past validation.

alternatives.option: Stage the worktree index directly and restore each path afterwards.
alternatives.reason: The restore ran only on the paths the author predicted: a validation exception exited the dry run with the staged index still installed and quiet intent-to-add, symlink and mode-only entries leaked through.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A future staging design proves path-by-path restoration complete over intent-to-add, assume-unchanged, skip-worktree and mode-only entries under concurrent edits.

alternatives.option: Commit the first baseline without staged-tree validation.
alternatives.reason: An unvalidated commit records whatever the worktree holds, including concurrent edits and hook interference, with attribution attached — the false baseline the packet exists to prevent.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Validation becomes unavailable in a context where an attributed baseline is still required and the developer explicitly accepts unvalidated adoption.

consequences: Baseline adoption, the Git staging runner and the cache helper all take an optional private index; the per-path restore machinery and its tests are removed; dry runs validate without changing anything.
context: Validating the first baseline of a converted tree requires staging content and judging the staged tree without letting a refusal, dry run or validation exception leave the staged index installed or swallow a concurrent edit.
decider: Architect private-index ruling under developer direction D147, executed through the owner admission cases for the R14 successor.
